items.label: f06-diagnostic-design
items.front: Chapter 17: how to design a diagnostic event before writing the log line
items.back: Start from a question, not a log statement: write down the decision the log should support (for example, will retrying completion create another version). Correlation ids connect records but do not say whether a record was written before or after its operation, so name events at precise boundaries: metadata-save-attempted, metadata-save-confirmed, dispatch-attempted, dispatch-returned. Avoid one 'completed' event emitted before the remaining effects; after a crash, a missing log is ambiguous.

items.label: f03-worked-change-files
items.front: Worked change: what each main file gained.
items.back: UploadSession: integer ceiling + int.MaxValue guard, SHA-256 format check, EnsureOpen, ExpectedChunkSize. UserStorageAccount: overflow-safe EnsureCanReserve. UploadChunk: changed-duplicate check before storage, expected size passed in, conflict -> 409. CompleteUpload: preflight -> assemble -> length -> digest -> blob -> graph -> reserve -> one save. Hashing: returns HashedContent(Checksum, Length).

items.label: f08-read-model-portfolio
items.front: Chapter 16: a test portfolio for the search read model
items.back: A direct query fixture: owner separation, deleted visibility, name match, extracted-text match, no match, current-version projection. A provider-backed fixture: case behavior, ordering ties, translation. A multi-request scenario: inserts or deletes between pages. For performance, count queries and read the translated query plan before proposing an index, and keep wall-clock thresholds out of the first correctness suite in favor of structural evidence.

items.label: f04-evidence-by-boundary
items.front: Netdrop testing: which kind of test supplies evidence for which boundary
items.back: Domain tests for pure decisions (UploadSession rounding, strict SHA-256, overflow, final-chunk size, terminal states; UserStorageAccount quota and overflow): use concrete values and inspect state after the rejection, since a bare exception check would miss a method that mutates before throwing. Real filesystem tests for publication (FileSystemChunkStorageTests in unique temp directories): the winner is the actual accepted file, not a mock call count, and cleanup targets only the fixture's own directory.

items.label: f09-storage-conformance-fixture
items.front: Chapter 15: rules for a safe blob-storage conformance fixture
items.back: Use an explicit new temporary directory with synthetic bytes only. Supply three custom streams: one that throws after a known prefix, one that counts reads, one that blocks on a test-controlled gate (no random sleeps). Scope cleanup to the fixture's own directory and never take a repository storage root as an implicit default; fail if the path already exists. For S3, a request-recording fake shows request construction (bucket, key, stream, token), not remote durability.

items.label: f02-atomicity-resources
items.front: Concepts: what does each atomic step actually protect?
items.back: The filesystem non-overwriting move protects the chunk path; EF SaveChanges groups tracked DB changes; neither covers the external blob write plus the queue call. The code won't delete a content-addressed blob after an uncertain DB failure, because another upload may share the key.

items.label: f10-guard-matrix-first
items.front: Chapter 09: how to centralize file-operation guards without breaking behavior
items.back: First write a matrix of the owner, parent, name, deletion and scan checks each operation needs (create, rename, move, copy, delete, restore, upload completion), marking absent checks as source observations rather than confirmed remote defects. Then find missing or inconsistent rules. A shared destination policy must fit each operation (creating a child cannot form a cycle the way moving an ancestor can; a copied file has no subtree), and a helper should implement an agreed policy, not hide differences behind a generic ValidateNode.

items.label: f01-completion-order
items.back: Exact index set -> quota preflight (EnsureCanReserve) -> assemble -> compare length -> compare digest -> blob find-or-create -> file node -> version + scan job -> Reserve -> session.Complete -> one SaveChanges -> delete chunks -> enqueue.

items.label: f07-safe-diagnostic-fields
items.front: Chapter 17: safe diagnostic fields, metric labels and timing
items.back: Never log bearer tokens, share tokens, passwords, raw file content or full extracted text; use internal ids, bounded error categories, content length and approved metadata (even file names need a decision). High-cardinality ids belong in traces or structured logs, not metric labels; count by phase and outcome. Use a monotonic timer for durations and UTC timestamps for cross-system correlation, remembering clock skew.

InMemory does not enforce the SQL unique index, so a fixture seeding the same chunk twice fails SingleOrDefault: a fixture mistake, not an application defect.

items.prompt: Per chapter 09, what does DeleteAsync do when a user deletes a folder that has children?

choices.text: Moves the node into a hidden trash folder that the janitor empties

items.explanation: Chapter 09 line 33: DeleteAsync marks the node deleted and saves; it does not recursively delete descendants, remove blob bytes or release quota. RestoreAsync clears the flag without checking for a new sibling with the same name. Trash is a node-level state, and what that means for descendants is left as a product question.

A service test can prove which stream was opened but not completed delivery, the middleware has no Response.HasStarted guard, and AccessCount cannot tell complete from partial transfers.

The concepts guide is explicit: neither boundary makes the queue call part of one global transaction, and the code deliberately avoids deleting a content-addressed blob after an uncertain failure.

items.explanation: Chapter 14 lines 25-27 warn that a SingleAsync missing row raises a different exception from the explicit not-found AppException branch. In code, the Status action calls SingleAsync (UploadsController.cs line 26), which throws InvalidOperationException when no row matches. ExceptionMiddleware (lines 17-29) maps AppException to its own status, DomainException to 400 and UnauthorizedAccessException to 401; everything else, this exception included, becomes a 500 with the detail hidden. SingleAsync never returns null, there is no EF-to-409 rule, and no DomainException is involved.

The handler passes that size through IChunkStorage.StoreAsync's expectedSize parameter (IChunkStorage.cs line 16); the filesystem adapter itself is not in git at this pin and survives only as a snapshot under astraupskill/snapshots/.
